original_question: Which severe complication of the varicella-zoster virus is characterized by symptoms such as dizziness, dysarthria, hemiparesis, and paresthesia?

final_qi.question: Which severe complication of the varicella-zoster virus is characterized by symptoms such as dizziness, dysarthria, hemiparesis, and paresthesia?
final_qi.search_keyword: varicella-zoster virus severe complication dizziness dysarthria hemiparesis paresthesia
final_qi.long_answer: The symptoms described—dizziness, dysarthria, hemiparesis, and paresthesia—are indicative of a stroke, particularly an ischemic stroke. Varicella-zoster virus can lead to a severe complication in the form of a cerebrovascular event. When VZV reactivates, it may cause inflammation of the cerebral blood vessels (vasculopathy), which can result in an ischemic stroke. This process disrupts normal blood flow to parts of the brain and produces the neurologic deficits mentioned.

candidate.long_answer: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) can lead to serious complications involving the central nervous system. One such severe complication is VZV vasculopathy, which can result in a cerebrovascular accident (stroke). In this condition, the virus induces inflammation in the blood vessels supplying the brain, leading to either ischemic or hemorrhagic events. The resulting stroke manifests with numerous neurological deficits such as dizziness, dysarthria (difficulty speaking), hemiparesis (weakness on one side of the body), and paresthesia (abnormal sensations).
